text:
Dear Dr. Vance,

Thank you for agreeing to evaluate this young boy, whose difficulties first became apparent during infancy with pervasive developmental delays across cognitive, speech, and motor milestones. In addition, his linear growth has remained stunted, tracking well below the third centile, although his head circumference has tracked steadily along the 50th percentile. His family history is non-contributory, and his routine immunizations are up to date.

On examination, he exhibits a distinct craniofacial pattern. I noted widely set eyes, bilateral eyelid drooping, an increased distance between the inner canthi, and a shortened nasal length with forward-facing, upturned nostrils. The philtrum is elongated; it is neither broad nor short. His extremities show shortened digits, fixed flexion deformities at the proximal interphalangeal joints, mild cutaneous webbing between adjacent fingers, and an unbroken single horizontal palmar crease, alongside generalized peripheral joint hyperlaxity. 

His abdomen demonstrates an unusually prominent, protruding navel, though there is definitely no umbilical hernia. Inguinal canals are intact without any inguinal hernia. Genitourinary inspection reveals bilaterally undescended testes and scrotal tissue that wraps saddle-like over the anterior base of the penis. The urethral meatus is orthotopic at the tip of the glans with no evidence of hypospadias. 

Cardiovascular examination is reassuring with crisp heart sounds and no murmurs; an early screening echocardiogram specifically ruled out any ventricular septal defect, and his chest is clear to auscultation bilaterally.

Given this constellation of physical traits and early-onset developmental concerns, I would be most grateful for your expert clinical evaluation and guidance regarding further management.

Warm regards,

Dr. Eleanor Hayes
Community Pediatrics
